question_text: Complete the sentence with the correct preposition: The customs were searching _____ drugs at the airport.
explanation: Search for — to look for something.

question_text: Insert the correct preposition: He acceded _____ my request.
explanation: Accede to — to agree to a request.

question_text: A synonym of the word 'Equivocal' is—
explanation: Equivocal means ambiguous.

question_text: They are men of like build and stature. In this sentence 'like' has been used as a/an—
explanation: 'Like' modifies 'build and stature'.

question_text: Fill in the blank: He could not _____ to see his brother in any kind of distress.
explanation: 'Bear' means tolerate.

question_text: Which response is correct for the statement 'I like ice-cream'?
explanation: 'So do I' agrees with a positive statement using a main verb.

question_text: A _____ of wolves.
explanation: A pack of wolves.

question_text: Study the sentence: Come and meet me in my office. What part of speech is 'me'?
explanation: 'Me' is a pronoun.

question_text: The feminine gender of Drone is—
explanation: A drone is a male bee.

question_text: Replace the underlined portion with an idiom: I begged him to reconsider his decision but he refused to yield.
explanation: 'Put his foot down' means to refuse firmly.

question_text: What is the most appropriate passive form? The mason is building the wall.
option_a: The wall is being built by the mason.
option_b: The wall is been build by the mason.
option_d: The mason is built by the wall.
explanation: Present continuous passive: is/are being + past participle.

question_text: An antonym of the word 'Magnanimous' is—
explanation: Selfish is opposite in meaning to magnanimous.

question_text: He replied that he worked whenever he liked. This is a/an—
explanation: The sentence contains a subordinate clause.

question_text: Replace the underlined verb with an appropriate phrasal verb: The building was demolished last year.
explanation: Pull down means demolish.

question_text: Change into an affirmative sentence: This story is incomplete.
option_c: Completeness is there in this story.
explanation: The printed answer is B; verify the source's semantic equivalence before publication.

question_text: Replace the underlined verb with an appropriate phrasal verb: The plan did not succeed.
explanation: Come off can mean succeed.

question_text: Change the voice: The guard refused him admittance.
option_a: The guard refused to let him in.
option_b: Admission was not granted to him by the guard.
option_c: He was not admitted by the guard.
option_d: He was refused admittance by the guard.
explanation: Passive construction retains 'admittance' as object.

question_text: Replace the underlined word with the appropriate idiom: He listened when his boss spoke.
explanation: 'Was all ears' means listened attentively.

question_text: An ophthalmologist deals with—
option_b: diseases related to the respiratory system.
explanation: An ophthalmologist specializes in eye diseases.

question_text: Fill in the blanks: A man _____ live _____ satisfactorily _____ he does at present _____ half his present income.
explanation: Printed answer: can, as, as, on.

question_text: Replace the underlined portion with an idiom: He got himself into trouble by interfering in his neighbour's affairs.
explanation: 'Burnt his fingers' means suffered through involvement.

question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct modal verb: The online store informed that we _____ cancel the order we placed, if we wish.
explanation: Printed answer: can.

question_text: Replace the underlined verb with the appropriate phrasal verb: I have stopped smoking.
explanation: Give up means stop a habit.

question_text: What kind of sentence is this? The moon was bright and we could see our way.
explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'and'.

question_text: The adjective form of the word 'Glory' is—
explanation: Glorious is an adjective.

question_text: Choose the correct alternative: The car broke down and we _____ get a taxi.
explanation: Past-tense obligation: had to.

question_text: Replace the underlined verb with the appropriate phrasal verb: He has quarrelled with her.
explanation: Fall out with someone means quarrel.

question_text: Fill in the blank: The _____ half of the play was uninteresting.
explanation: Latter refers to the second of two parts.

question_text: Change the voice: All his friends laughed at him.
option_a: He was laughed at by all his friends.
option_c: His friends were laughing at him.
option_d: He laughed at all his friends.
explanation: Passive of 'laughed at' retains the preposition.

question_text: Life is as tedious as a twice-told tale. The figures of speech used in the sentence are—
explanation: Printed answer: Simile and Alliteration.
